complexity.notes: The intervals.pop(i+1) inside the while loop shifts the tail of the list, so each removal is O(n) and up to n removals makes the whole merge O(n^2) even after the O(n log n) sort. Building a fresh result list instead of popping would fix that. Since the input is guaranteed sorted, sorting is unnecessary: ||a single linear pass that copies intervals ending before newInterval, merges all overlapping ones into it, then copies the rest|| runs in O(n) time. Also note the code mutates and returns a list containing the caller's original interval objects, and `List` needs `from typing import List` (or use builtin `list` generics).
complexity.summary: Appends the new interval, sorts everything by start, then merges overlapping intervals in a single pass, popping merged elements in place. Correct, but it discards the given invariant that intervals is already sorted.
